lead.hed: A Washington Guard battalion linked drones to mortar crews at Yakima
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Sept. 23: soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 161st Infantry, trained with fire supporters at Yakima Training Center during their Sept. 17-19 drill. The photo was taken Sept. 18. Lt. Col. Josh Brown said the aim was to put unmanned aircraft into the chain that finds a target and directs fire. Drill report, not a deployment order.
lead.image_credit: Photo courtesy of Sgt. 1st Class Zach Molhoek · DVIDS 9961362 · Public domain · Washington Army National Guard soldiers conduct mortar training at Yakima Training Center, Sept. 18, 2026.

political.hed: U.S. F-35s join an Indian air exercise starting Saturday
political.insight: Defense News, Friday, from New Delhi: Air Force F-35s will fly in India's Tarang Shakti drills at Jodhpur, the first time the jet undertakes tactical missions with Indian fighters from an Indian base. Eight countries are participating. The exercise runs Saturday through Oct. 12. Announced participation, not a sale.

political.hed: The administration scrapped a Biden-era power-plant rule
political.insight: Heritage, Monday: four years of rules made affordable electricity harder to produce and raised prices. The commentary says the Trump administration then scrapped a Biden-era power-plant rule. Commentary, not a new statute.

political.hed: A Friday essay traces the friendship behind U.S. religious-freedom law
political.insight: Public Discourse, Friday: Thomas Farr writes that Frank Wolf and Chris Smith met in Bucharest in 1985 and later wrote the 1998 International Religious Freedom Act and the 2016 Frank Wolf revision. The Religious Freedom Institute will give them this year's Defender of Religious Freedom award. Essay, not a new statute.

tech.hed: A Thursday essay says unlimited politics will not settle the data-center fight
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Thursday: the piece treats local anger over data centers as a test of the liberal state, and argues that politics without limits is not the answer to discontent over the technological build-out. Essay, not a zoning vote.

tech.hed: Students are picking Southern colleges the way families pick Southern jobs
tech.insight: Heritage, Monday: the commentary says families are choosing colleges the way they already vote and move. It says North Carolina gained students in 2025, and that the map of higher education is being redrawn with a Southern accent. Commentary, not an enrollment census. Not a ship story.

culture.hed: A review of Sam Brownback's book on China's war on faith
culture.insight: WORLD, posted Thursday: the review covers China's War on Faith, co-authored by former ambassador-at-large Sam Brownback. It says bishops are held under house arrest, pastors are imprisoned, and people in the pews are sent to reeducation camps. Review, not a new State Department designation.

culture.hed: A review says some churches treat losing as the proof of faithfulness
culture.insight: American Reformer, Monday: Alex Kocman reviews D. Michael Clary's Loser Theology. The argument is that suffering and the cross are real, but they do not make striving, building, or winning suspect. Book review, not a church ruling.
